svg.text: CVA6 Suite 7: WAW Hazard Resolution (Out-of-Order Execution vs In-Order Commit)
DIV a0,gp,tp (FLU multicycle) vs LI a0,99 (ALU single-cycle) targeting same rd=x10
Microarchitectural Analysis of WAW Hazard Resolution:
1. Execution Completion Out-of-Order: "LI a0, 99" finishes execution in 1 cycle, while "DIV a0, gp, tp" takes 8 cycles in the integer divider unit. Both target architectural register x10 (a0).

2. In-Order Commit Guarantees Correct State: CVA6 Scoreboard retires strictly in FIFO order. DIV commits first writing quotient 100, and LI a0,99 commits second overwriting it with 99. Architectural state is never corrupted!
3. Consumer Routing (raw_checker.sv): "ADD a1, a0, zero" receives 99 because raw_checker points to the most recent producer in the scoreboard (last_before_idx), ignoring the earlier DIV instruction.
